fmri.pipeline

fmri.pipeline is an R package for specifying, running, and tracking task fMRI general linear models with FSL, AFNI, and SPM. Use the same trial, run, and participant tables to generate suite-specific designs and contrasts, then run them locally or on a cluster.

The package is built around a single analysis object, usually called gpa, that stores the input tables, model specifications, output locations, backend choices, scheduler settings, and job-tracking state for one analysis.

Current package version: 0.5.

Why this package exists

Large fMRI GLM projects have a familiar failure mode: the actual analysis is a constellation of design files, shell scripts, scheduler jobs, and partially remembered choices. fmri.pipeline tries to make that constellation explicit. The package helps you:

  • define run-level, subject/session-level, and group-level models in one place;
  • generate backend-specific analysis files for FSL, AFNI, and SPM;
  • submit staged analyses through Slurm, TORQUE, or local execution;
  • keep track of job dependencies, logs, and analysis status;
  • reuse the same input tables and YAML model specification across model revisions;
  • support longitudinal analyses where runs are nested within sessions and sessions are nested within subjects.

Choose an engine with glm_software = "fsl", "afni", or "spm" in setup_glm_pipeline(). FSL fits runs separately and can carry their variances into higher-level models. AFNI estimates shared task effects across runs. SPM models runs as separate SPM sessions by default and can contrast their coefficients within one first-level model. The GLM engine guide follows a two-run task through each suite and shows where to inspect its design and contrast maps.

fmri.pipeline is not a preprocessing pipeline. It expects preprocessed 4D BOLD NIfTI files, event timing, and optional confound files from tools such as fMRIPrep, custom preprocessing workflows, or lab-specific derivatives.

Analysis structure

The package uses a stable three-level vocabulary:

  • Level 1 fits the BOLD time series using trial events, signals, and nuisance regressors.
  • Level 2 combines run-level contrasts in multi-run FSL analyses. SPM and AFNI handle the runs within L1.
  • Level 3 models subject or subject-session contrast maps across participants.

Models are organized as sets at each level. For a multi-run FSL analysis, two compatible models at each of the three levels yield eight combinations. For native AFNI or SPM, select the L1 and L3 models to run.

Input data

The preferred setup uses three explicit long-form data frames:

Table One row per Purpose
trial_data trial/event Event onsets, durations, conditions, and trial-level modulators for Level 1 regressors.
run_data subject/session/run Paths to preprocessed run NIfTIs, run-level covariates, TR, confounds, and run exclusion flags.
subject_data subject or subject/session Level 3 covariates. For longitudinal analyses, use one row per id + session.

Default identifier columns are id, session, and run_number. If your project uses different names, pass a named vm vector to setup_glm_pipeline().

For BIDS-like derivatives, helper functions can create starter tables:

run_df <- generate_run_data_from_bids(
  bids_dir = "/proj/lab/derivatives/fmriprep",
  task_name = "taskname",
  desc = "preproc",
  suffix = "bold"
)

subject_df <- generate_subject_data_from_bids(
  bids_dir = "/proj/lab/derivatives/fmriprep"
)

trial_df <- generate_trial_data_from_bids(
  bids_dir = "/proj/lab/derivatives/fmriprep",
  task_name = "taskname"
)

Treat these helpers as a starting point. In most real analyses, you will still join in task variables, exclusions, and study-specific covariates before submitting the pipeline.

Basic usage

Install from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("HallquistLab/fmri.pipeline")

Create the analysis object from explicit input tables:

session_data is not a user-provided input; setup_glm_pipeline() derives gpa$session_data internally from run_data and subject_data.

library(fmri.pipeline)

gpa <- setup_glm_pipeline(
  analysis_name = "facehouse_longitudinal_demo",
  scheduler = "slurm",
  output_directory = "/proj/lab/glm_outputs",
  subject_data = subject_df,
  run_data = run_df,
  trial_data = trial_df,
  glm_software = c("fsl", "afni"),
  n_expected_runs = 4L,
  l1_models = NULL, l2_models = NULL, l3_models = NULL,
  confound_settings = list(
    motion_params_file = NULL,
    confound_input_file = NULL,
    spike_volumes = NULL
  )
)
gpa$level_backends <- list(l1 = "fsl", l2 = "fsl", l3 = c("fsl", "afni"))

Define models interactively:

gpa <- build_l1_models(gpa)
gpa <- build_l2_models(gpa)
gpa <- build_l3_models(gpa)

export_glm_config(gpa, file = "task_glm_spec.yaml")

Or build the model sets from a YAML specification:

gpa <- build_l1_models(gpa, from_spec_file = "task_glm_spec.yaml")
gpa <- build_l2_models(gpa, from_spec_file = "task_glm_spec.yaml")
gpa <- build_l3_models(gpa, from_spec_file = "task_glm_spec.yaml")

Run selected model combinations:

run_glm_pipeline(
  gpa,
  l1_model_names = "facehouse",
  l2_model_names = "l2_id_session",
  l3_model_names = c("l3_pooled_subject_ev", "l3_3dlmer_session")
)

Check status and inspect logs:

diagnose_pipeline(gpa)
view_log(gpa, level = 1, id = "01")

Estimation by engine

FSL

glm_software = "fsl" is the default. FEAT fits one time-series model per run. For a multi-run analysis, build an L2 model to combine the run COPEs and their VARCOPEs. Set l2_scope = "id_session" when the group model needs one estimate per visit. With a single run, L1 feeds L3 directly. Inspect the generated .fsf files, the run’s .feat/stats/ directory, and the higher-level .gfeat outputs.

AFNI

Select glm_software = "afni" in setup_glm_pipeline() to use AFNI throughout the analysis. Build L1 and L3 models with the usual YAML specification, then submit them with:

run_glm_pipeline(
  gpa,
  glm_software = "afni",
  l1_model_names = "all",
  l2_model_names = "none",
  l3_model_names = "all"
)

AFNI estimates one model per subject/session. All retained runs share task coefficients; each run has its own polynomial baseline and nuisance coefficients. It always uses the pipeline’s convolved regressors, preserving event durations, parametric modulators, and signal normalizations. Runs with exclude_run = TRUE and excluded subjects do not enter the fit. This is a joint time-series fit: AFNI does not run a separate L2 job or apply L2 model specifications. Use FSL’s explicit L2 path when you need run-level COPE/VARCOPE combination or L2 contrasts.

Configure AFNI through glm_settings when creating the pipeline:

glm_settings = list(afni = list(
  estimation = "REML",        # default; "OLS" uses 3dDeconvolve alone
  polort = "A",               # AFNI automatic run drift order, or an integer >= 0
  mask = NULL,                # optional mask on the input image grid
  censor_column = "afni_censor_file",
  write_residuals = TRUE,
  force_l1_creation = FALSE,
  force_l3_creation = FALSE
))

When run_data$afni_censor_file is supplied, each path points to a single-column binary vector (1 = keep, 0 = censor). Censor files and nuisance files may contain either retained volumes or original volumes with the specified leading drops. Length mismatches fail setup. Spikes on retained volumes remain nuisance regressors. The AFNI design drops spike columns that become empty after censoring. Without an explicit mask, L1 intersects masks derived from the retained runs. Image geometry must match; AFNI estimation does not perform registration or intensity normalization. Supply preprocessed images in a common space and on a comparable intensity scale.

L3 uses ordinary least squares for the pipeline’s group design and contrasts, through 3dDeconvolve with no temporal baseline or prewhitening. per_session analyses stay separate by session; pooled_sessions_subject_ev retains the pipeline’s subject effects. For longitudinal mixed models, specify l3_input_mode: 3dlmer. AFNI-only analyses use AFNI contrasts as group inputs. To retain a hybrid workflow, set execution_backend: afni and producer_backend: fsl on the L3 model and select FSL at L1/L2. Existing mixed FSL/AFNI 3dlmer configurations continue to default to FSL inputs.

Outputs live under afni_l1/ and afni_l3/ (mixed models use afni_3dlmer/). Each ordinary GLM directory contains run_afni_glm.sh, afni_glm.log, design.xmat.1D, stats.nii.gz, a mask, and optional residuals. contrasts.tsv maps original contrast names to con_####.nii.gz and tstat_####.nii.gz; regressors.tsv maps names to AFNI labels. Completion requires both the success marker and every expected output. Failed jobs return a nonzero status to the scheduler. After changing event/model specifications, set force_l1_creation = TRUE to rebuild the cached design, then rerun setup and estimation.

Resource settings are under gpa$parallel$afni: l1_glm_time, l1_glm_memgb, l1_glm_cpus, l1_glm_alljobs_time, and the corresponding l3_glm_time, l3_glm_memgb, l3_glm_cpus. Existing l3_lmer_* settings continue to control mixed models. Configure AFNI modules or PATH through parallel$compute_environment$afni.

AFNI’s 3dDeconvolve documentation and 3dREMLfit documentation describe the OLS and REML estimators.

SPM

Set glm_software = "spm" and give glm_settings$spm$spm_path the path to your SPM installation. The default first-level design treats each run as an SPM session and creates one SPM.mat per participant, study visit, and task model. Build the L1 and L3 models and submit with l2_model_names = "none". Pipeline L3 is the SPM second-level analysis.

SPM L1 contrasts are matched to the fitted design by regressor name. A missing required regressor or a non-estimable contrast stops the job. Group inputs are selected using the actual SPM.xCon names recorded in spm_contrasts.tsv, so a change in contrast order cannot silently select a different effect.

SPM setup checks retained scan counts and nuisance rows against each run’s run_volumes and drop_volumes. Original images use the appropriate leading scan offset; already-trimmed images start at scan 1. Nuisance files may contain original or retained rows. Missing files and inconsistent lengths are errors. Compressed images use separate temporary paths for each analysis and run.

A complete SPM fit needs a successful full run and validated, nonempty model, beta, contrast, statistic, and requested residual files. Setup records the model specification and input signatures in spm_setup.rds; images use path, size, and modification time, while nuisance files are content-hashed. Rerun setup_l1_models() or setup_l3_models() after changing inputs or model settings. Existing fits without the new validation metadata require setup and estimation once before they can be reused. Runs with disabled setup, estimation, or contrast stages receive a stage-completion marker and remain incomplete for group input selection.

YAML model specifications

The model builders read the model sections of the YAML file. Set the analysis-wide glm_software and level_backends in R as shown above. The analysis block below records those choices alongside the face/house model definitions:

analysis:
  name: facehouse_longitudinal_demo
  scheduler: slurm
  glm_software:
    - fsl
    - afni
  level_backends:
    l1: fsl
    l2: fsl
    l3:
      - fsl
      - afni
  n_expected_runs: 4

onsets:
  - onset

durations:
  - duration

events:
  stim:
    onset: onset
    duration: duration

signals:
  face:
    event: stim
    trial_subset_expression: object == 'face'
    normalization: none
    value_fixed: 1

  house:
    event: stim
    trial_subset_expression: object == 'house'
    normalization: none
    value_fixed: 1

l1_models:
  facehouse:
    signals:
      - face
      - house
    contrasts:
      diagonal: true

l2_models:
  l2_id_session:
    level: 2
    l2_scope: id_session
    model_formula: ~ stress_label
    reference_level:
      stress_label: stress
    contrasts:
      diagonal: true
      cond_means:
        - stress_label
      pairwise_diffs:
        - stress_label
      overall_response: true

l3_models:
  l3_pooled_subject_ev:
    level: 3
    l3_input_mode: pooled_sessions_subject_ev
    execution_backend: fsl
    producer_backend: fsl
    model_formula: ~ session_label
    reference_level:
      session_label: analgesic
    diagonal: true
    cond_means:
      - session_label
    pairwise_diffs:
      - session_label
    overall_response: true

  l3_3dlmer_session:
    level: 3
    l3_input_mode: 3dlmer
    execution_backend: afni
    producer_backend: fsl
    model_formula: ~ session_label
    random_effects: (1 | Subj)
    reference_level:
      session_label: analgesic
    diagonal: true
    cond_means:
      - session_label
    pairwise_diffs:
      - session_label
    overall_response: true

This example demonstrates the current longitudinal pattern: keep runs nested within subject-session at Level 2 (l2_scope: id_session), then fit either an FSL-native session model with subject explanatory variables or an AFNI 3dLMEr model using FSL-produced Level 2 inputs.

Output layout

Each analysis is written under output_directory/analysis_name. The exact layout depends on selected backends, but typical outputs include:

analysis_name/
  configuration_files/     # exported specs, caches, and finalized pipeline objects
  scheduler_scripts/       # one batch_<uuid>/ folder per run_glm_pipeline() call
  feat_l1/                 # FSL Level 1 setup and outputs
  feat_l2/                 # FSL Level 2 setup and outputs
  feat_l3/                 # FSL Level 3 setup and outputs
  spm_l1/                  # SPM first-level analyses
  spm_l3/                  # SPM group models
  afni_l1/                 # AFNI subject/session fits
  afni_l3/                 # AFNI ordinary group GLMs
  afni_3dlmer/             # AFNI 3dLMEr data tables, scripts, and outputs
  logs/                    # text and JSON logs
  glm_pipeline.sqlite      # job tracking database

The pipeline writes backend preflight information before submission, then tracks submitted jobs through the SQLite database. diagnose_pipeline() summarizes the job tree and helps locate failed or incomplete stages.

FSL group models can include an inference configuration to run pTFCE automatically after L3 estimation:

gpa$l3_models$models$group$inference <- fwe_spec(
  "group_ptfce", targets = list(l3_model = "group"),
  fwe_alpha = 0.05, two_sided = TRUE
)
run_glm_pipeline(gpa, l3_model_names = "group")

The L3 model builder offers the same settings, and export_glm_config() preserves them in YAML. FWE is controlled separately within each selected map. Use run_fwe_correction(gpa) to retry correction without fitting models again, and refresh_fwe_correction(gpa) to collect scheduled results. See the FWE vignette for custom masks, resource settings, and the standalone planning workflow.

Longitudinal workflows

Longitudinal fMRI analyses require special care because runs, sessions, and subjects represent distinct sources of variation. The current recommended patterns are:

  • For multi-run FSL, use l2_scope = "id_session" to keep one L2 estimate per visit. Native AFNI L1 already produces one fit per visit. SPM preserves that distinction with its default l1_session_mode = "separate".
  • Use l3_input_mode = "pooled_sessions_subject_ev" for balanced categorical visit comparisons that should remain inside FSL.
  • Use l3_input_mode = "3dlmer" for irregular visits, incomplete follow-up, continuous time effects, treatment-by-time interactions, or random-effects structures that are better handled by AFNI 3dLMEr.
  • In FSL, reserve l2_scope = "id" for cases where sessions are essentially pseudo-runs and longitudinal change is not the target.

The longitudinal vignette walks through a face/house study with repeated visits.

MEDuSA deconvolution, event-locked alignment, and multilevel trajectory modeling (mixed_by, jlmer, meta_mixed_by) now live in the standalone medusa package. Legacy pre-0.4-1 MEDuSA entry points in fmri.pipeline emit deprecation warnings and forward to medusa when installed.

End-to-end tests

The clock-task suite runs FSL, SPM and AFNI from trial data through group contrasts on Slurm. It includes a four-participant smoke profile and the complete 80-run fixture. Run the clock GLM suite.

Development status

fmri.pipeline is under active development. For new projects, prefer YAML model specifications, explicit subject_data/run_data/trial_data tables, and small test runs before launching the full model grid.

Issues and feature requests are tracked at https://github.com/HallquistLab/fmri.pipeline/issues.
